issues.legal_issue: Joint heirs who merely receive income from inherited assets do not constitute an association of persons for income-tax assessment unless they join in a common purpose or action to produce income.
material_facts: Three widows inherited an estate as joint tenants, each entitled to an equal share of its income.
The shares were registered separately in the names of the widows, and there was no finding that they jointly managed them.
The widows jointly received dividends and interest but did no act that helped produce that income.
issues.conclusion: The widows were not an association of persons in respect of the income at issue, and the assessment of that income on that basis was not valid.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, an association of persons requires two or more persons to join in a common purpose or common action, with the object of producing income, profits or gains. It must be a combination formed to promote a joint enterprise for producing income. Mere joint receipt of income is insufficient. The Court approved the tests in In re B. N. Elias, Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Laxmidas Devidas, and In re Dwarakanath Harishchandra Pitale; whether an association exists depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.

rule.if: income_tax_assessment_proceeding and joint_heirs and jointly_received_income and not joint_income_producing_action

predicates.income_tax_assessment_proceeding: The matter concerns the assessment of income for income-tax purposes.
predicates.joint_heirs: Two or more people inherited property together and were entitled to share its income.
predicates.joint_income_producing_action: The co-heirs acted together in a way that helped produce income.

issues.definition: When joint heirs are assessed for income tax, jointly receiving income without acting together to produce it results in their income not being assessed as that of an association of persons.

issues.legal_issue: Income from inherited property with definite and ascertainable equal shares is not assessable as income of an association of persons where the statutory rule for property income applies.
material_facts: The widows inherited immovable property and each was entitled to one-third of its income.
The Appellate Assistant Commissioner had held that section 9(3) applied to the property income, and the Department did not appeal that finding.
The Tribunal treated the widows’ shares as indefinite and reversed that result; the Supreme Court stated that their shares were definite and ascertainable and that section 9(3) applied.
issues.conclusion: The property income was subject to section 9(3), and the Tribunal was wrong to treat the widows’ shares as indefinite and assess that income as belonging to an association of persons.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(3) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, applied to income from property where the co-heirs’ shares were definite and ascertainable. The Court also held that the Tribunal could not go behind the unappealed finding of the Appellate Assistant Commissioner that the section applied.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_proceeding: The matter concerns the assessment of income for income-tax purposes.
predicates.property_income: The income being assessed arises from property held by more than one person.
predicates.co_owners_have_definite_ascertainable_sh: Each co-owner’s share of the property income is definite and ascertainable.
predicates.prior_property_income_finding_not_appeal: An earlier appellate finding applied the separate property-income treatment, and that finding was not appealed.

issues.definition: When property income is assessed, definite and ascertainable co-owner shares and an unappealed earlier finding for separate treatment result in the property income being assessed separately.
